title: SSE chunk-certificates for safe fragment reassembly and proactive reconnect negotiation
creator: Evelyn Park
description:
Problem: Resuming server-sent-event (SSE) streams across disconnects is brittle for interleaved tool/function calls and structured outputs. Current resume-token approaches are prone to ambiguous boundaries when fragments are emitted concurrently (toolcall frames + content frames), which forces conservative client-side buffering and complicates deterministic reassembly for private deployments.

Proposal (high-level): Introduce a compact per-chunk 'chunk-certificate' that travels in-band with SSE fragments (as a short metadata line or header envelope). Each certificate contains: stable chunk_id, sequence_offset, provenance_hash (short), model_variant, toolcall_boundary flag, checkpointable flag, and a short lease_id. Certificates are HMAC-signed with a per-tenant key (rotatable) to prevent tampering.

Key capabilities:
- Deterministic reassembly: clients can validate the provenance_hash and chunk_id to stitch fragments in order even if they arrive out of order or are re-sent.
- Ambiguity-free toolcall detection: toolcall boundaries are explicitly marked, eliminating heuristics around JSONL boundaries.
- Proactive reconnect negotiation: on SSE handshake the server can advertise a certificate window and short-lived lease tokens. Clients reconnecting present last-seen certificate id + lease token; server grants a delta replay or direct resume. Servers may also pre-issue certificate windows when generation stalls to avoid long replay periods.
- Backwards compatibility: include compatibility header X-RW-SSE-CERT-V1; if absent, server falls back to resume-token-only mode. Clients can negotiate downgrade to token-only if they detect intermediate proxies that strip extra metadata.

Design trade-offs:
- Metadata cost vs correctness: certificates add ~40-120 bytes per fragment (configurable). We'll make certificates optional and enable via header/feature-flag to limit cost for high-throughput workloads.
- Cryptographic overhead: HMAC verification per certificate is cheap but non-zero; we will batch-verify on the client path where feasible and provide an option for trust-mode within private deployments.
- Storage & retention: servers must retain certificate windows for lease durations (tunable TTL). This requires slight state retention per connection but avoids global token issuance for every message.

Implementation notes:
- Wire format: newline-prefixed JSON-lite envelope with base64-compact fields to keep SSE lines human-readable but small. Example envelope: :cert:eyJpZCI6IjEiLCJzIjoxMiwicGgiOiJhbWZ...
- Handshake: client sends Accept: application/sse+cert; server responds with X-RW-SSE-CERT-V1: window=[cid:1-256],lease=abc123,alg=HMAC-SHA256
- Resume flow: reconnect includes Last-Cert: cid=125;Lease: abc123; server returns replay_start=126 or issues a delta window.
- Toolcall handling: toolcall frames include certs with toolcall_boundary=true. When a toolcall is re-sent the cert id is preserved so idempotency checks are easier.

Security & ops:
- Key management: use tenant-scoped HMAC keys stored in KMS; rotate with overlap window to avoid invalidating short-lived leases.
- Observability: emit metrics for cert verification failures, replay fallbacks, and per-tenant certificate overhead. Add traces for handshake and resume latencies.

Why different from resume-token-only approaches: certificates provide chunk-level provenance (hash+id) rather than a stream position token. This reduces ambiguity on interleaved frames and improves deterministic client reassembly for structured outputs and tool calls.
acceptance_criteria: Clients can resume an SSE stream using chunk-certificates and reassemble toolcall + content frames deterministically
Fallback to resume-token-only when header absent or when intermediaries strip metadata
Certificate verification failures are recorded and do not cause silent data corruption; clients surface explicit error and fallback to token replay if possible
Perf regressions at p95 latency < 2% for typical generation workloads when certificates enabled (configurable rollout)
Integration tests simulating out-of-order deliveries, duplicated fragments, and mid-toolcall disconnects pass deterministically
Canary rollout controlled by header/feature-flag and circuit-breaker that reverts on >0.5% increase in malformed-fragment rate
rollout_plan: 1) Feature gated behind Accept header and org-level feature flag. 2) Deploy server-side support behind runtime-1.22 feature flag, enable certificate generation for 5% of internal traffic. 3) Ship lightweight client library change (SDK opt-in) using offline verification and replay helpers. 4) Canary to customer-facing hosted API with 1% traffic, observe metrics for 24h, expand to 25% if green, then full opt-in. 5) Provide 'trust-mode' for private deployments to skip HMAC verification for performance (documented risk).
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for envelope encode/decode, HMAC sign/verify, and certificate windowing.
- Integration harness that injects re-ordering, duplication, and drop events between server and client.
- Chaos tests: kill connection during active toolcall emission and validate deterministic reassembly on resume.
- Load test: measure p50/p95/p99 latency and CPU for HMAC signing at expected QPS (scale up to Dedicated capacity profiles).
- Backwards compatibility tests with legacy clients that only support resume-token protocol.
- Fuzz testing the base64 envelope to ensure we handle proxy mangling gracefully.
comments: 2025-02-21 - Spike: implemented prototype encoder/decoder in Python. Verified ~80 bytes avg metadata and correct reassembly for interleaved toolcall scenario.

2025-02-24 - Design review with runtime and SDK teams. Decision: use HMAC-SHA256, base64-compact payload, and optional enable via Accept header. Action: create KMS key rotation plan and storage TTL for certificate windows.
2025-02-27 - Eng note: prototype caused ~1.6% increase in p95 under small-batch cases; we'll implement batching of verification on SDK path to mitigate.
2025-03-01 - PR #3456 opened: server generation + handshake + unit tests. Needs integration tests and security review sign-off.
2025-03-03 - Security review requested (ticket SEC-1287). Primary concerns: key rotation overlap, replay window abuse; added rate-limiting to lease issuance and documented TTLs.
Reviewer feedback (2025-03-03): make envelope resilient to line-oriented proxies by adding an alternate header-based carrier for environments that strip colon-prefixed SSE comments.
